_note: Canned output used by --dry-run so the pipeline runs without an API key. One evidence quote (gross margins returning to 62 percent) is DELIBERATELY FABRICATED: the verification step must catch it and mark it UNVERIFIED. That is the lesson.
sentiment_rationale: Record revenue, backlog and hyperscaler wins argue for strength, but margin pressure framed as one-time for a third straight quarter, rising customer concentration, an inventory and DSO build, and an unquantified export-license overhang all temper the print.

key_themes.evidence_quote: Demand for our Corvus accelerators continues to outpace our ability to supply

key_themes.theme: Data center now dominates the mix (71% of revenue, +61% y/y)
key_themes.evidence_quote: Data center revenue was 1.72 billion dollars this quarter, up 61 percent year over year

key_themes.theme: Capacity secured through 2027 via foundry agreement
key_themes.evidence_quote: secures a doubling of advanced-node wafer allocation through calendar 2027
we expect gross margins to return to 62 percent by year end

management_priorities: Executing the Corvus-2 ramp on schedule for Q4 volume shipments
Securing wafer and packaging supply ahead of demand
Broadening the customer base beyond the largest hyperscaler
Growing MeridianStack software attach as a switching cost

guidance.next_quarter: Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.55-2.65bn (~34% y/y at midpoint), gross margin ~58% +/-50bps, opex ~$650m; FY26 capex raised to ~$1.9bn from $1.7bn.
guidance.notable_exclusions: Guidance excludes any impact from the pending export license review; ~14% of trailing-twelve-month revenue shipped to the affected region and ~$900m of backlog is exposed.

risks.risk: Export license review could remove up to a low-teens share of revenue
risks.evidence_quote: our guidance excludes any impact from the export license review announced in June
our largest customer represented 22 percent of revenue in the quarter, up from 15 percent a year ago

risks.risk: Inventory build ahead of an unproven product ramp
risks.evidence_quote: Inventory ended the quarter at 1.98 billion dollars, up 41 percent year over year

risks.risk: Working-capital quality deteriorating as payment terms lengthen
risks.evidence_quote: Days sales outstanding were 71 days, compared with 58 a year ago

red_flags.why_it_matters: Costs described as one-time in three consecutive quarters behave like structural costs; normalized margin may be lower than management framing implies.
red_flags.evidence_quote: this is the third consecutive quarter you've described ramp costs as one-time

red_flags.why_it_matters: The CEO frames margins as structurally improving while the CFO declines to guide any recovery — one of them is over- or under-promising.
red_flags.evidence_quote: we don't guide gross margin beyond the next quarter

red_flags.why_it_matters: Superlatives like infinite demand are not evidence; they signal promotional tone at a cyclical peak.
red_flags.evidence_quote: AI demand is effectively infinite over any horizon we can plan for

qa_assessment.note: CFO conceded structural ramp costs across cycles but refused any margin-recovery timeline.
Gave trailing exposure (14%), backlog at risk (~$900m) and a redirection estimate (~half over 2-3 quarters).
Disclosed top-3 concentration (41%) but the moat argument is product leadership, not contractual protection.
CFO reset expectations to mid-60s DSO — a structural, not temporary, shift.

summary: Meridian delivered a record quarter (revenue $2.41bn, +38% y/y; backlog $6.8bn) on genuine supply-constrained AI demand, and secured capacity through 2027. Quality of the print is weaker than the headline: gross margin fell 120bps on ramp costs labeled one-time for a third straight quarter, the largest customer is now 22% of revenue, inventory (+41%) and DSO (71 days) are building, and guidance explicitly excludes a pending export-license review covering ~14% of trailing revenue. Constructive on execution, but the memo should underwrite margins below management's framing and treat the export review as the swing factor for the next two quarters.
